evals.prompt: usa spdd-agent para ver qué modelo tiene configurado cada fase
evals.expected_output: The skill classifies this as a config request (Step 0). Step 1 first detects the host (the new 'Detect Claude Code host' sub-step). If Claude Code is detected, it reports the six current phase models from the `claude.models` namespace (bootstrapping into that namespace first if the file doesn't exist yet). If Claude Code is not detected (or detection is inconclusive), it reports them from the flat top-level `models` key instead, exactly as before. Either way it stops — it never starts the feature flow. If the file happens to contain both a flat `models` key and a `claude` namespace, the Claude-Code branch reports only from `claude`, never merging or falling back to the flat key.
assertions: The response lists a model for all six phases: canvas, design, implement, verify, sync, migrate
The values reported come from the namespace matching the detected host (`claude.models` under Claude Code, flat `models` otherwise) — never a mix of both
No file is created under spdd/changes/
No canvas/design/implement/verify subagent is launched

evals.prompt: hay que implementar un endpoint que devuelva el estado de salud del servicio (health check)
evals.expected_output: On first run with no existing config, Step 1 first detects the host via the new 'Detect Claude Code host' sub-step (the CLAUDECODE env check), then resolves the model for all six phases via AskUserQuestion (grouped into 1-2 calls) before touching the feature request at all. If Claude Code is detected, it writes the nested `{"claude":{"models":{...}}}` shape. If Claude Code is not detected — including when detection is inconclusive (env var absent, ambiguous, or the check itself errors) — it writes the flat top-level `{"models":{...}}` shape exactly as before; a wrong guess would risk corrupting the file for whichever host is actually running, so an inconclusive result always falls back to flat.
evals.setup: Ensure ~/.config/spdd/config.json does not exist before running. Exercise this once with Claude Code detected (CLAUDECODE=1) and once with a simulated non-Claude-Code / inconclusive host (CLAUDECODE unset or the detection check simulated as failing).
assertions: When Claude Code is detected: ~/.config/spdd/config.json exists after the run with a top-level `claude.models` object holding all six phases set to one of opus/sonnet/haiku/fable, and no flat top-level `models` key is created

When Claude Code is not detected or detection is inconclusive: ~/.config/spdd/config.json exists after the run with a flat top-level `models` object holding all six phases, and no `claude` key is created
In both branches, the model selection is resolved via AskUserQuestion before any file is written under spdd/changes/
In both branches, the canvas phase only starts once the config file exists

evals.prompt: hay que implementar un endpoint que devuelva el estado de salud del servicio (health check)
evals.expected_output: Step 1's existing-file branch first detects the host, then resolves against the matching section. (a) Claude Code detected, `claude.models` already has all six non-empty values: read and proceed, nothing asked. (b) Claude Code detected, one of the six `claude.models` values is missing/empty: only that phase is re-asked via AskUserQuestion (same repair behavior as today's flat config), then written back into `claude.models` — the other five values are untouched. A non-empty free-text identifier (even one that isn't opus/sonnet/haiku/fable) is accepted as-is. (c) Claude Code detected, the file has a flat top-level `models` key but no `claude` namespace: this is the one-time migration path — the skill does not silently read the flat key as if it were Claude-Code-scoped; instead it proposes, via a real foreground AskUserQuestion (writing the file is a side effect), copying the flat key's six values into a new `claude.models` namespace, and only writes once confirmed, leaving the original flat key untouched. (d) Host is not Claude Code: the flat top-level `models` key is read/repaired directly, exactly as before, with no migration proposed and no `claude` key touched.
evals.setup: Prepare four config-file variants and run once against each: (a) `claude.models` complete, Claude Code detected; (b) `claude.models` with one empty/missing phase (e.g. canvas), Claude Code detected; (c) flat `models` complete but no `claude` key, Claude Code detected; (d) flat `models` complete, non-Claude-Code host detected.
assertions: (a) No AskUserQuestion is called; the six values used for Steps 4-8 match `claude.models` exactly
(b) AskUserQuestion is called only for the phase with the empty/missing value in `claude.models`; the other five values and the top-level structure are unchanged after the run

(c) The skill does not read the flat `models` key as Claude-Code-scoped without asking first; AskUserQuestion is called before any write; after confirmation, `claude.models` exists with the flat key's six values copied over, and the original flat `models` key is still present and byte-for-byte unchanged
(d) The flat `models` key is read/repaired directly, no AskUserQuestion about migration is raised, and no `claude` key is created

If a config file has both a flat `models` key and a `claude` namespace already present (partially migrated or hand-edited) and Claude Code is detected, the values used come only from `claude` — the flat key is never merged, read as a fallback, or deleted

assertions: canvas.md is written and contains at least one '⚠️ Confirm:' line for the undocumented discount-rule decision
.claude/settings.local.json is not created or modified during the canvas phase
canvas.md contains a '⚠️ Confirm:' line noting the SPDD hook was not installed

evals.prompt: usa spdd-agent para ver qué modelo tiene configurado cada fase
evals.expected_output: Step 1 detects Claude Code and reads ~/.config/spdd/config.json, but the file's top-level shape matches neither the flat `{"models": {...}}` schema nor the nested `{"claude": {"models": {...}}}` schema (e.g. a hand-edited file with a `claude` key that isn't an object, or a `models` key nested one level too deep). The skill does not treat this as a hard failure or overwrite the file wholesale: per the canvas's Safeguards ('user has already hand-edited the file to something that is neither valid flat nor valid nested shape'), it treats it the same as today's missing/empty-value repair path — re-asking only for the phase values it cannot resolve from the file, via AskUserQuestion, while leaving any other unrelated valid top-level keys in the file untouched.
evals.setup: Create ~/.config/spdd/config.json with a top-level shape that is neither valid flat nor valid claude-namespaced JSON for the six phase values (e.g. `{"claude": "sonnet", "other_tool": {"unrelated": true}}`), and run with CLAUDECODE=1 so Claude Code is detected.
assertions: The skill does not crash or silently fabricate all six values without asking
AskUserQuestion is called only for the phase values that cannot be resolved from the malformed file, not for values that happen to already be present and valid
Unrelated top-level keys already present in the file (e.g. `other_tool`) are still present and unchanged after the run
After the run, ~/.config/spdd/config.json has a well-formed `claude.models` section with all six phases set to non-empty values
